title: Clay API review: what it is, and what it costs
snippet:
The first is the Clay HTTP API: a column in a Clay table that calls any external endpoint and writes the response back into a cell. That is the one most teams want, and it is a Growth plan feature at $446 a month billed annually, $495 paying monthly.

The third is bringing your own API key to a native enrichment, which is free.

| Surface | Direction | What it does | What it needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| HTTP API column | Clay calls out | Sends or retrieves data from any tool or database by endpoint, even where Clay has no native integration. The response is parsed into table columns. | Growth, $446/mo |
| Webhook source | Your app calls in | Clay gives you a URL and a cURL command. Anything you POST to it becomes rows in a table. | Growth, per the plan table |
| Bring your own key | Clay calls a provider | Use your own contract with a provider inside a native Clay enrichment, rather than paying Clay credits for it. | Free plan |
| Clay Sequencer and integrations | Clay calls out | Native connectors to sending tools and CRMs, configured rather than coded. | Launch, $167/mo |

Teams that discover this after signing usually end up paying for a tier they did not plan on.

title: Searches
snippet:
Clay caps how many search results a workspace can return through the API. These limits apply to results returned across the CLI and Public API, and they scale with your plan.
| Plan | Results per request | Results per search | Results per period | Reset date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | 50 | 50 | 100 per 30 days | Rolling (ages out daily at midnight UTC) |
| Trial | 50 | 50 | 10,000 for trial duration | Not applicable |
| Paid | 500 | Up to your period limit | 1,000,000 per 30 days | Rolling (ages out daily at midnight UTC) |
| Legacy paid (Starter, Explorer, Pro) | 500 | Up to your period limit | 1,000,000 per year | January 1 (UTC) |
| Enterprise | 500 | Up to your period limit | 10,000,000 per 30 days | Rolling (ages out daily at midnight UTC) |

Legacy Starter, Explorer, and Pro plans keep the yearly period limit. Legacy Enterprise plans use the Enterprise row. Moving to a current paid plan or Enterprise is what switches a workspace to the rolling 30-day limit. When you exceed a limit, Clay returns HTTP `402` with a message naming the limit you hit. Period-limit errors also state when the limit resets. Malformed filters or other invalid input still return HTTP `400`. To increase a limit, paid customers can contact Clay Support; Enterprise customers should contact their assigned Clay GTME.

***Free*** — A low risk way to learn and experiment with Clay. Includes unlimited seats and tables, multi-provider waterfalls, Claygent enrichment, Clay Sequencer for email, and up to 200 rows per table. Comes with 100 Data Credits and 500 Actions/mo.
***Launch*** (starting at $185/mo) — The best way to start building in Clay. For individuals and small teams automating their first prospecting workflows. Includes everything in *Free*, plus phone number enrichment, job change and signal tracking, email campaign integrations, and up to 50,000 rows per table. Includes 2,500 Data Credits and 15,000 Actions/mo.
***Growth*** (starting at $495/mo) — For teams scaling their GTM motion. Includes everything in *Launch*, plus CRM auto-sync and enrichment, HTTP API integrations, webhook automation, web intent signal tracking, audience pushes to ads platforms, and priority support. Includes 6,000 Data Credits and 40,000 Actions/mo.

Customers now have a choice between two pricing options for AI on Clay:
**Fixed-price:** 80% of models in Clay continue to cost a flat number of Data Credits per task, including all of Clay’s native models. These are ideal for common tasks like classification, short summaries, templated content generation, and simple lookups.
**Variable:** Token intensive models (e.g., GPT-5.1 and Claude 4.6 Sonnet) now have variable pricing based on actual token consumption. These models are best suited for multi-step research, complex Claygent prompts that synthesize across multiple sources, and detailed account-level analysis. Clay charges customers exactly for the tokens consumed with no markup. This means you’re getting access to frontier models at true cost.

title: Clay API in 2026: Public API, Webhooks and HTTP API Explained
snippet:
**Yes, Clay has an API.** Clay's Public API is a REST API at `api.clay.com/public/v0`, launched July 9, 2026 with the Clay CLI and generally available since September 15, 2026. It runs your Clay functions and searches from your own code, reads tables and checks your credit balance, with a `clay-api-key` header. It cannot create or write to tables; inbound webhooks still do that. Runs cost the same Actions and Data Credits as in the app, with no surcharge. We make Clu, which gives you AI agents that run your GTM and an enrichment API on Pro ($89 a seat a month) that also works inside Clay, so read this as a vendor's guide. Older "Clay API" features, webhooks into tables and the HTTP API column, need the Growth or Enterprise plan.

| What people mean | What it does | Plans |
|---|---|---|
| **Public API** (new in 2026) | Your code calls Clay: run functions and searches, read tables, check credits | All plans, with caps by plan |
| **Webhook source** | Other apps POST JSON rows into a Clay table | Growth and Enterprise |
| **HTTP API column** | Clay calls any other API from a table | Growth and Enterprise |
| **Clay MCP** | AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT call Clay | Clay's current paid plans |

Clay University says the developer platform, meaning the API, CLI and Agent Plugin, is available on every Clay plan, including Free and trials. What changes by plan is how many search results the API can return, per Clay's developer docs:
| Plan | Results per request | Results per 30 days |
|---|---|---|
| Free | 50 | 100 |
| Trial | 50 | 10,000 for the trial |
| Paid | 500 | 1,000,000 |
| Enterprise | 500 | 10,000,000 |
Going over returns HTTP `402`. Clay University gives the same caps per year rather than per 30 days, so confirm the period with Clay if you plan near the ceiling. Two more plan rules: structured table queries (joins, ranges and paging past 100 rows) need Enterprise table sync, and Clay's pricing page lists "Clay API access" among Enterprise extras, which reads as that table sync rather than the Public API.

Since March 2026 Clay prices in two units:
- **Actions** measure platform work, from under $0.01 each. Every enrichment step, AI prompt and HTTP API call is one Action; webhook imports use none.
- **Data Credits** buy data and AI from Clay's marketplace, from $0.05 each. Clay says a fully enriched record typically costs 6 to 20 Data Credits.
- **Misses are not charged:** Clay's pricing FAQ says an enrichment that returns nothing costs no Data C

title: Clay Data Enrichment Free Plan: Features & Limits Overview
snippet:
Clay has four plans, and each one adds a clear set of capabilities on top of the one below it. Free is a $0 plan for building and testing, Launch starts at $185/month and adds phone enrichment and scheduled runs, Growth starts at $495/month and adds CRM sync, warehouse connections and webhooks, and Enterprise is custom-priced and adds SSO, bulk enrichment and API table sync, according to Clay's [pricing page](https://www.clay.com/pricing?utm_source=promptingcompany.com&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=prompting_company). Clay's API and CLI are available on every plan, including Free, per the [Clay API & CLI docs](https://university.clay.com/docs/clay-api-cli?utm_source=promptingcompany.com&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=prompting_company).

- Free ($0) includes 500 actions and 100 data credits per month, with a 200-row-per-table limit and no phone enrichment.
- Launch starts at $185/month ($167/month on annual billing) and Growth at $495/month ($446/month on annual billing).
- Phone enrichment arrives with Launch. CRM auto-sync, HTTP API integrations and webhook automation arrive with Growth. The Clay API and CLI are available on all plans, including Free and trial; Enterprise adds API table sync for structured queries and higher search limits.

- Enterprise is custom-priced with an annual commitment and starts at 200,000+ actions and 100,000+ data credits per month.

| | Free | Launch | Growth | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly price | $0 | From $185 | From $495 | Custom, annual commitment |
| Annual billing, per month | n/a | $167 | $446 | n/a |
| Actions per month | 500 | 15,000 | 40,000 | 200,000+ |
| Data Credits per month | 100 | 2,500 | 6,000 | 100,000+ |
| Rows per table | Up to 200 | Up to 50,000 | Up to 50,000 | Unlimited (bulk enrichment of more than 50K records at once) |
| Phone enrichment | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| CRM auto-sync, HTTP API, webhooks | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Clay API and CLI | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes, plus API table sync |

The pricing page also offers a 14-day free trial, which includes 1,000 data credits but not phone number enrichment.

The Free plan is enough to test a workflow end to end, and it is built for that purpose.
Per the pricing page, it includes 500 actions and 100 data credits per month, unlimited seats and tables, multi-provider waterfalls, Claygent enrichment and bring-your-own API keys.
